sentences.text: By this application under section 378(4) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, the applicant seeks special leave to appeal against the judgement and order of acquittal dated 30.4.2012 passed by the learned Chief Judicial Magistrate, Palanpur in Criminal Case No.4399 of 2006.

Mr. K. L. Pandya, learned Additional Public Prosecutor assailed the impugned judgement and order by submitting that the learned Judge has failed to appreciate the evidence in proper perspective and has erroneously come to the conclusion that the prosecution has not established the charges levelled against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.
It was submitted that the prosecution has led voluminous evidence, both documentary as well as oral, against the accused and has duly established the charges levelled against them.
Under the circumstances, the matter requires consideration and the leave, as prayed for, deserves to be granted.

sentences.text: A perusal of the impugned judgement and order reveals that the learned Judge has held that the prosecution has not established the charges levelled against the accused on various grounds.
However, considering the view that the court is inclined to take in the matter, it is not necessary to set out all the findings recorded by the learned Judge.
It may be noted that in the present case, the food article in question is R.M.D. Brand Gutkha.
A sample thereof was collected by the Food Inspector, Palanpur on 23.2.2006.

A perusal of the report of the Director, Central Food Laboratory, Mysore reveals that the lable of the R.M.D. Gutka reflected the following :
RMD GUTKHA Ingredients Betelnuts, Catechu, Tobacco, Lime, Saffron, permitted spices and flavour contain added flavour, Mfd.

By Dhariwal Industries Ltd., N. H.
No.8, Fazalpur, Post: Sankarda, Dist. Baroda 391 350 (Gujarat); Batch No.-C; Pkd.
On -2/2006; Best before within six months from the date of packing; Veg. Symbol Given; Net Wt. of 50 pouches is 100g; Statutory warning Given.

The record of the case reveals that after the sample of the food article in question was taken by the Food Inspector, a portion thereof was sent to the Public Analyst,
Vadodara for analysis thereof.
As per the report of the Public Analyst, the sample was found to be adulterated and misbranded.
After the lodging of the complaint, the accused No.1 made an application dated 21.8.2006 for sending a sample thereof for analysis to the Central Food Laboratory.
It appears that the sample ultimately came to be forwarded to the Central Food Laboratory only on 15.11.2007.

The Central Food Laboratory, thereafter, submitted its report dated 19.12.2007 opining that GUTKHA (RMD BRAND) does not conform to the general safety standards laid down for AN ARTICLE OF FOOD under the provisions of PFA Act, 1954 & Rules thereof in that,
(a) the sample contains Magnesium carbonate, an anticaking agent, which is not allowed under Rule 62 of PFA Act.
From the facts recorded hereinabove, evidently the food article in question was packed on 2.2.2006 and the shelf-life thereof was a period of six months from the date of packing.

Admittedly, the sample was forwarded for testing only on 15.11.2007,
that is, much after the shelf-life of the food article in question had expired.

Under the circumstances, in the light of law laid down in various judgments of the Supreme Court in this regard, the accused have been deprived of their valuable right under section 13(2) of the Food Adulteration Act, 1954 of getting the sample tested by the Central Food Laboratory.

True it is that the Director, Central Food Laboratory has opined that the sample was in a condition fit for analysis, however, the very fact that the shelf-life of the food article in question had expired, is indicative of the fact that the sample could not have been in a fit condition for analysis.
Under the circumstances, the accused having been deprived of their valuable right under section 13(2) of the Act, the entire proceedings stand vitiated.

The learned Judge was,
therefore, justified in holding that the prosecution has not established the charges levelled against the accused beyond reasonable doubt.

Leave is, therefore, refused and the application is rejected.
